label: Logbook notes written for this app in Morphy's voice, from public 1858-59 tour facts and games in his PGN. Morphy wrote no book.

notes.text: Arrived in England in the summer of 1858 hoping for a match with Mr Staunton. The match never came. I played the London men instead, and I recorded wins against Boden, Bird, Medley and Owen. Develop, sir, and the rest follows.
Herr Loewenthal and I played a proper match in London. He is a fine player; I won it. What I remember is how often a single tempo in the opening decided the afternoon.
At Birmingham I gave a simultaneous exhibition and played many boards at once. Mr Lyttelton among them. One learns to see a position whole when there is no time to stare at it.

The Café de la Régence in Paris. Gaslight, mirrors, and the whole city watching. I played eight gentlemen there blindfold in a single sitting. Count your developed pieces; it is cheaper than counting your mistakes.
Herr Anderssen came to Paris in December and we played our match. He attacks like a storm; I tried only to be developed before the storm arrived. I won the match.

At the opera in Paris I played the Duke of Brunswick and Count Isouard in consultation. A short game. Open lines, every piece out, and the queen sacrificed at the end. Pieces at home do not defend anything.
Home again in 1859, with exhibitions in New York. They gave me a watch and a chessboard. Of the evening I recall mostly the boards, as one does.
